title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ export tooling
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: This PR adds an automatic defaults layer for batching and KV-prefix caching, a set of calibrated quantization profiles for common model families, and a small unit-economics export tool used by SRE/finance to estimate per-token cost under autotuned configs. Motivation: production customers are seeing large variance in unit cost depending on batching/caching settings and quantization choices; this work lets the runtime pick conservative defaults and provides tooling for teams to evaluate trade-offs.

What this PR includes (high level):
- runtime/autotuner: new autotune controller that observes latency percentiles, batch sizes, and cache hit rates and proposes defaults
- config/defaults.yaml: new schema for batching/caching defaults and per-model family quant profiles
- runtime/quant_profiles/: profiles for gpt-family, llama-family, mixtral variants with FP16/INT8 options and fallback rules
- tooling/unit_econ/exporter.py: command-line tool to export per-route/unit-econ CSVs for finance and alerting
- docs/optimization/autotune.md: user-facing doc describing defaults and how to opt-out
- tests/{unit,integration}: added coverage for autotune heuristics and quant profile selection

Checklist: 
- [x] Autotune controller implementation
- [x] Conservative defaults applied at config load time
- [x] Quant profiles for top-4 families
- [x] Unit/econ exporter with CSV output and a small summary table
- [x] Integration tests simulating mixed request sizes and cache priming
- [x] Docs and release notes

Commits summary: see commits field for short messages; CI passed on final squash.

Files touched (high-level):
- runtime/autotuner.py (new): implements observe -> propose -> apply loop; small snippet: def propose(self, metrics): return ProfileSelection(recommended_batch=metrics.p50_batch*1.2, cache_ttl=600)
- runtime/kv_cache.py: wired cache hit metrics into autotuner
- config/defaults.yaml (new): added batching.default_window, caching.prefix_ttl_seconds, model.quant_profile
- runtime/quant_profiles/gpt-family.yaml (new) and llama-family.yaml (new)
- tooling/unit_econ/exporter.py (new): --route / --model-family flags, writes CSV to stdout
- docs/optimization/autotune.md: new doc describing behavior and opt-out
- tests/autotune_test.py, tests/quant_profile_selection_test.py

Notes on behaviour and safety: default profiles are conservative (prefer slightly larger batches to improve throughput while enforcing soft latency SLOs). INT8 quant profiles include a dynamic fallback to FP16 if output-quality regression exceeds a small threshold in the eval harness. These thresholds are encoded in config/defaults.yaml under model.quality_tolerance_pct.

Impact and rollout plan: The change is behind a feature flag (autotune.enabled=false by default for hosted customers). We enabled the flag for internal Dedicated accounts and ran a 2-week canary (see ENG-5123). Once canary metrics stabilized (p95 latency within target, median cost reduction ~12%), we flipped the default for internal Dedicated and made the feature opt-in via project config for hosted customers. Rollout controlled via rollout/autotune-config.

CI summary: initial lint failure on config schema (fixed in follow-up commit), integration tests flaky on cache priming (additional wait added), final CI run: all checks passed (unit/integration/lint/security-scan).

Related work: Linear ENG-5123 (autotune rollout), ENG-5231 (quant profiles for model onboarding). Support case SUP-1284 prompted adding the exporter tool.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals from Diego, Priya, and Evan. Post-merge tasks: schedule a run of the unit-econ exporter across top-20 customers and add an alert if cost increases >5% for any route.
